units.text: It reads and writes PDF documents, supports form filling and field manipulation, extracts text and images from pages, and creates new documents with text, tables, and interactive elements.

Build pages from scratch or edit existing ones with Page and Paragraphs, laying out tables (Table, Row, Cell), floating boxes (FloatingBox), headers and footers (HeaderFooter), and text, image, or page-number stamps (TextStamp, ImageStamp, PageNumberStamp), and draw shapes and gradients directly on a page with Line, Rectangle, Circle, Arc, Curve, Ellipse, and GradientAxialShading.
Locate, extract, and replace text across a document with TextFragmentAbsorber and TextAbsorber, including right-to-left and Arabic glyph shaping via ArabicShaper.

Work with AcroForm fields — TextBoxField, CheckboxField, ComboBoxField, ListBoxField, RadioButtonField, and SignatureField — through Form, plus XFA forms via XfaForm, including JavaScript and FormCalc scripting and conversion to AcroForm with XfaAcroFormConverter and XfaFlattener.

Add and read annotations — highlight, underline, strikeout, and squiggly markup, free text, ink, stamps, file attachments, links, and redaction — through Annotation subclasses such as HighlightAnnotation, FreeTextAnnotation, InkAnnotation, StampAnnotation, FileAttachmentAnnotation, LinkAnnotation, and RedactionAnnotation.

Sign documents with PKCS#7 (RSA, DSA, or ECDSA) via PdfSigner, PKCS7, and PKCS7Detached, and verify existing signatures with SignatureVerificationResult, while encrypting and decrypting documents with AES or RC4 via AESCipher, RC4Cipher, and StandardSecurityHandler, with separate user and owner passwords.
Split, merge, insert, extract, and reorder pages with PdfFileEditor, and edit individual page size and rotation with PdfPageEditor.
Validate and convert documents to PDF/A-1 through PDF/A-4 with PdfAValidator, PdfAConverter, and PdfAValidationResult.
Import HTML into a PDF with HtmlLoadOptions and HtmlToPdfConverter, and export a PDF back to HTML or XML with HtmlSaveOptions, PdfToHtmlConverter, and SaveFormat.

The central class is Document, whose pages are reached through PageCollection and Page, each backed by a Resources dictionary. Document-level convenience operations are exposed through the facades — PdfFileEditor, PdfContentEditor, PdfBookmarkEditor, PdfExtractor, PdfConverter, and PdfFileSignature, among others.
The org package root provides the foundational package namespace for the Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java module.
The org.aspose package namespace contains the core API types for working with PDF documents, including Document, Page, and PageCollection.
The org.aspose.pdf package namespace contains the full public API surface for Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java, including core types, annotations, devices, drawing, and form handling.

Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java reads and writes PDF documents, supports HTML and XML conversion, and provides basic text extraction and annotation capabilities. It targets Java 11 and is distributed as the org.aspose:aspose-pdf-foss package at version 26.9.0.

OCR of text in scanned images, conversion to non-PDF formats beyond HTML and XML, conversion from non-PDF formats beyond HTML, full XFA form rendering, and 3D annotations or PRC/U3D streams are not supported.
The PdfFileSecurity.setAllowExceptions method throws UnsupportedOperationException because the legacy AllowExceptions=false toolkit-key-size path is not implemented.
Text replacement with non-Latin scripts (CJK, Arabic, Hebrew) supports basic cases, but complex bidirectional reordering and shaping edge cases may differ from a reference renderer.
Resource optimization supports basic stream recompression, but advanced strategies such as image downsampling profiles and font merging across resources are limited.
Tagged PDF and logical structure is readable and supports programmatic construction of structure trees, but coverage for building fully well-formed structure trees is partial.
PDF/X validation and conversion supports PDF/X-1a:2001 and PDF/X-3 through the same Document.validate and Document.convert API used for PDF/A, but this path has no dedicated test coverage yet.
